answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency Rule. At each dawn, an identity’s actions from prior epochs are hashed into a persistent profile; new behaviour must fall within a bounded divergence of it or the identity is flagged and throttled. Divergence thresholds are derived per agent from a stable basalt anchor record fixed at registration, preventing profile resets. Each flagged identity must then submit a prism decomposition—independent traces proving the behaviour originates from distinct, non-duplicated controllers.
